abstract: The distinctiveness of people with chronic illness as storytellers is how they experience their illness. Symptoms, pain, and biological disruptions are eloquent forms of speech of the body that beget social articulation. The stories people tell about illness shape how suffering is legitimized, and acted upon. Large language models have emerged as new mediators within this landscape---a role once predominantly supported by communities. In doing so, these systems participate in what we term narrative translation: transforming lived illness experiences for particular audiences and purposes. Through 21 prototype-driven semi-structured interviews with people with chronic illness, we contribute an empirical account of how participants navigate this mediation alongside existing sources of support. Our findings surface distinct yet complementary roles participants envisioned for AI and their communities, and how trust in AI was shaped by learning model-boundaries and perceiving understanding. We characterize these findings to inform future designs of AI-mediated narrative support.

ob.ai_reason: LLM作为慢性病叙事中介，AI核心议题，属HCI边缘相关
ob.tldr: 研究慢性病患者如何借助大语言模型与社群进行疾病叙事的转译，即把亲身病痛经历转化为面向不同受众的表达。通过21位患者的原型驱动半结构访谈，发现AI与社群承担互补角色：AI作为新的中介者参与叙事转译，信任建立于学习模型边界与感知理解程度之上。揭示了人机协同叙事支持的设计启示。

ur.ai_reason: 21次半结构访谈，慢病叙事与AI中介
ur.tldr: 基于21位慢性病患者的原型驱动半结构访谈，研究LLM如何参与"叙事翻译"——将身体化的疾病经历转译给特定受众。揭示患者赋予AI与社区以互补角色：AI承担信息整合与受众适配等翻译劳动，社区提供情感支持与真实性校验。信任的建立取决于用户能否感知模型能力边界与是否感受到被理解，为AI中介的叙事支持设计提供启示。

title: The Labor of Storytelling: How People with Chronic Illnesses Leverage AI and Communities for Narrative Translation
title_zh: 叙事的劳动：慢性疾病患者如何借助AI与社群实现叙事转译
